description: Four-voice oscillator fed by one 1V/OCT jack, handing each new pitch to a different voice by one of four assignment rules

params.text: Shifts the pitch of all four voices together, ±5V read as one volt per octave with 0V giving C4; moving it never reassigns pitches between voices
Shifts the pitch of all four voices together by up to 100 cents either way; moving it never reassigns pitches between voices
Sets every voice to a sine wave
Sets every voice to a triangle wave
Sets every voice to a square wave
Sets every voice to a sawtooth wave
Each new pitch goes to voice 1 and pushes the older pitches along, voice 1 to voice 2, voice 2 to voice 3 and voice 3 to voice 4
Each new pitch goes to the next voice up, and after voice 4 back to voice 1
Each new pitch goes to the next voice up until voice 4, then to the next voice down until voice 1, and so on back and forth
Each new pitch goes to one of the four voices picked at random

inputs.text: The pitch handed out to the voices, one volt per octave; one voltage is read, not polyphonic channels

outputs.text: The chosen wave at voice 1's pitch, swinging ±5V
The chosen wave at voice 2's pitch, swinging ±5V
The chosen wave at voice 3's pitch, swinging ±5V
The chosen wave at voice 4's pitch, swinging ±5V

notes: a pitch is only handed to a voice once the voltage at 1V/OCT has held the same value for two frames in a row, so a gliding or slewed input assigns nothing while it is moving.
the four output jacks are separate mono jacks, one per voice, and none of them carries a polyphonic cable despite the module being listed as polyphonic.
all four voices sound all the time; with nothing patched to 1V/OCT they all play the pitch set by COARSE and FINE.

inputs.0:
1V per octave · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
